We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 5 reactions for target SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O.

We need to produce JSON route with 5 reaction steps. Use templates from database. We have found a template (664985) that seems to break a double bond and form a carboxylic ester? Actually that template seems to be a HWE? The result of apply_template gave precursors: ('C=C(O)/C=C/C=C/C[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)CO)O1', 'O'). So applying template 664985 to target gave two precursors: a molecule with a terminal carboxylic acid? Actually the precursor is C=C(O)/C=C/C=C/C[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)CO)O1 and O (water). That seems like a deprotection? Not sure.

We need 5 steps: likely include protecting group introduction (TBS), HWE to install side chain, DIBAL reduction, deprotection, etc.

We need to construct route: final target has a TBS protected? Actually target includes no silyl groups. So maybe we need to protect an alcohol earlier then later deprotect.

But we can propose any plausible route using available templates. We need to retrieve templates for each step.

We have templates for TBS protection (functional groups broken aliphatic hydroxyls, formed t-butyldimethylsilyl). We have template IDs 316813 and 394785 for protection. Use one.

We also need HWE (formation of double bond and ester). Search for functional_groups_broken ["C-C double bonds"] formed ["carboxylic esters"] gave template 664985. Use that as step maybe forward is HWE, retrosynthetic step would break the double bond and form ester? Actually forward HWE forms double bond and ester; retrosynthesis would break double bond to give aldehyde and phosphonate. But template 664985 seems to be a retro of HWE? It breaks double bond and forms ester? The description: functional_groups_broken C-C double bonds, formed carboxylic esters. So retro step: from product (ester with double bond) to precursor (maybe aldehyde + phosphonate). So we can use that.

We also need DIBAL reduction: functional_groups_broken maybe carbonyl? Actually DIBAL reduces ester to aldehyde (break C=O, form aliphatic hydroxyl?). Not sure.

We can search for functional_groups_broken ["carboxylic esters"] formed ["aldehydes"]? Let's try.
